description: Research agent collecting facts from 5 source documents about renewable energy

turns.content: Please analyze this source about solar energy: Solar panel efficiency has reached 26% for commercial panels in 2026. Installation costs have dropped to $2.50 per watt. Solar farms now provide 15% of US electricity generation.
From source 1, I extracted three key facts. Commercial solar panel efficiency is at 26% as of 2026. Installation costs are $2.50 per watt. Solar farms contribute 15% of US electricity generation.

Here is source 2: Wind energy capacity in the US reached 180GW in 2025. Offshore wind costs have dropped to $50 per MWh. Solar panel efficiency has reached 24% for commercial use, making it competitive with fossil fuels.

Source 2 provides wind energy data and a conflicting solar figure. US wind capacity is 180GW as of 2025. Offshore wind costs are $50 per MWh. Note: source 2 claims solar efficiency is 24%, contradicting source 1 which states 26%. The discrepancy may be due to different measurement standards.

Source 3: Battery storage costs fell below $100 per kWh in 2025. Lithium-ion remains dominant but sodium-ion batteries are gaining market share. Grid-scale storage capacity doubled year-over-year. Solar installation costs are approximately $2.50 per watt.

Source 3 covers energy storage developments. Battery storage costs are below $100 per kWh. Lithium-ion is the dominant technology but sodium-ion is an emerging competitor. Grid-scale storage capacity doubled in 2025. This source corroborates source 1 on solar installation costs at $2.50 per watt.

Source 4: The renewable energy sector employed 13 million people globally in 2025. Government subsidies for solar exceeded $20 billion worldwide. The biggest challenge remains grid integration for intermittent sources.

Source 4 addresses the policy and employment landscape. The renewable energy sector employs 13 million people globally. Government solar subsidies exceed $20 billion worldwide. Grid integration of intermittent sources remains the primary technical challenge.

Final source 5: Solar panel efficiency improvements have plateaued around 26% for silicon-based cells. Next-generation perovskite cells promise 30% efficiency by 2028. Wind energy is projected to reach 25% of US electricity by 2030.

Source 5 provides forward-looking data. Solar efficiency has plateaued at 26% for silicon cells, corroborating source 1. Perovskite cells may reach 30% efficiency by 2028. Wind energy is projected to supply 25% of US electricity by 2030. This is a notable growth target given the current 180GW capacity from source 2.
